BM25 and hybrid retrieval: what lexical ranking still buys you

BM25 remains the strongest single baseline for keyword retrieval. The scoring function rewards rare terms through inverse document frequency and saturates term frequency, so a page that repeats a keyword forty times does not outrank a page that uses it once, precisely where the query needs it.

In our benchmarks, a tuned BM25 index beat a small embedding model on exact-identifier queries, function names, product codes and quoted phrases. Embeddings win on paraphrase and on queries written in a different vocabulary from the document.

Hybrid retrieval

Hybrid retrieval runs BM25 and a dense retriever in parallel and fuses the ranked lists. Reciprocal rank fusion is the cheapest fusion rule and needs no score calibration between the two systems.

The practical lesson for a local-first search engine is that BM25 costs a few megabytes of memory and zero API calls, while a dense retriever costs a model download, a GPU budget or a hosted embedding endpoint.

Inverted index sizing

A compressed inverted index for one hundred thousand pages fits comfortably in memory on a laptop. Postings are delta-encoded, term frequencies are quantised, and the whole structure rebuilds in under a minute on commodity hardware.

If you are building offline search into a desktop agent, start with BM25, measure recall on your own queries, and only then decide whether a neural retriever earns its footprint.
